purpose: Aclidinium is used to help people with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) breathe more easily. It helps keep the airways in your lungs open so you can get more air in and out. It is a maintenance medication, meaning you use it every day to prevent breathing problems, not to treat a sudden attack.
how_it_works: Your airways have certain receptors that, when triggered, cause the muscles around them to tighten and narrow. Aclidinium blocks those receptors, which keeps the airway muscles relaxed and the airways open wider. Think of it like propping open a door so air can flow through more freely.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include headache, stuffy or runny nose, cough, and sore throat. Some people may also notice a dry mouth or diarrhea. These are usually mild and tend to get better over time.
warnings: Do not use aclidinium as a rescue inhaler during a sudden breathing attack — it will not work fast enough. Tell your doctor if you have glaucoma, trouble urinating, or an enlarged prostate, as this medicine may make those conditions worse. Contact your doctor right away if your breathing suddenly gets worse after using this medication. Avoid getting the spray in your eyes, as it may cause or worsen eye pressure problems.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is one inhalation (400 mcg) twice a day — once in the morning and once in the evening. Try to use it at the same times each day. Follow the instructions that come with your inhaler device to make sure you are using it correctly.
